answer: Every autonomous identity requires an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to access the network. This verifier maintains a registry where each record acts as a lotus of unique value, preventing identity duplication. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a massive cost asymmetry. The ledger functions like a lagoon of deep data, while any attempted address reuse triggers an echo of failure, resulting in an immediate, non-refundable slash. This fixed-burn mechanism ensures all participants remain distinct.
